messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: The study reports only system-level economic metrics (NPC, total investment, unit cost) for national-scale RO implementation and concentrate management. No PFAS removal, concentrate composition, or residual PFAS destruction metrics are presented in the cited text, so classifying the record as descriptive_only is consistent with the evidence (E05–E08).

The endpoint concerns economic evaluation (net present cost) of RO systems with evaporation ponds and incineration of sediments (E06, E07), not a physical or chemical treatment performance metric. Classifying it as 'other' is appropriate.
The endpoint is the treatment unit cost (USD/m3) for RO systems with evaporation ponds (E07), which is an economic metric. Classifying it as 'other' is appropriate.

E06–E07 describe NPC of RO systems and indicate that concentrate is managed via evaporation ponds and incineration of residual sediments; no PFAS removal or concentrate PFAS composition is quantified, matching the interpretation.
E07 reports treatment unit costs (USD/m3) for the system with an evaporation pond and notes dependence on landfill size; no PFAS treatment efficacy metrics are given, matching the interpretation.

The cited sections (E05–E07) focus on system design and economic modeling and do not report measured PFAS concentrations, removal efficiencies, or concentrate/residual properties, so this design-inferred limitation follows directly from the study design and reported content.

E05–E06 indicate that RO only separates PFAS into concentrate and that concentrate is disposed of via evaporation ponds and incineration of residual sediments; no PFAS destruction efficiency of incineration is quantified, so this design-inferred limitation is justified.

E08 states that PFAS-containing products are disposed of in municipal solid waste landfills, generating landfill leachate (LL) that is collected and treated in biological stabilization ponds at sanitary landfills, consistent with ‘landfill leachate (typically after biological treatment in stabilization ponds at sanitary landfills)’.

E05 describes a two-pass RO system with pretreatment and explains that wastewater passing through the RO membrane is divided into permeate (clean water) and concentrate with high salt/impurity concentrations including PFAS, matching the description.
No numeric unit is applicable for a qualitative configuration description; leaving the unit null is appropriate.
E08 reports that Thailand had 111 sanitary landfills; these are the landfills considered in the national-scale RO system planning (E06), so the value 111 is supported.
The field describes a count of landfills; a null unit is appropriate and consistent with the text (E08).
E06 states ‘111 sites with 8.2 mil· ton/yr. of total MSW’, matching the value 8.2 for municipal solid waste handled.
E06 gives ‘8.2 mil· ton/yr.’ for total MSW; the unit ‘million ton/yr’ is consistent with this notation.
E07 reports ‘the total estimated LL volume was 17.5 m3/yr.’, matching the numeric value 17.5 used in the record.
E07 specifies ‘17.5 m3/yr.’ as the total estimated LL volume; the recorded unit ‘m3/yr’ is correct.

E05 lists evaporation ponds as an appropriate concentrate treatment method for Thailand; E06 states that concentrate disposal by evaporation ponds and incineration of residual sediments was evaluated. The combined description matches these texts.
This is a qualitative description of a management method and does not require a numeric unit; leaving the unit null is appropriate.

E01 and E08 describe PFAS contamination in landfill leachate, with ranges from other studies but no specific PFAS species or compound-level resolution in this model. The summary that PFAS in LL are a concern and specific compounds are not resolved is accurate.
E07 reports ‘[SOURCE_TEXT_OMITTED sha256=727e431d485949acfcee3cf63d99673163cbe91c4148974708aff1fdbe6fedfd] evaporation pond’; the recorded value 577.9 matches exactly.
E07 expresses NPC as ‘577.9 mil. USD’; the unit ‘million USD’ is an appropriate and consistent representation of ‘mil. USD’.
E06 states ‘The total investment costs were approximately 578 mil. USD ... for the treatment systems with ... evaporation ponds’; the recorded value 578 matches this approximation.
E06 uses ‘mil. USD’ for total investment costs; the unit ‘million USD’ is consistent with this notation.
E07 reports ‘The treatment unit costs ranged from 1.72 – 2.71 USD/m3 for the system with an evaporation pond’; the lower bound value 1.72 is correctly captured.
E07 gives treatment unit costs in ‘USD/m3’; the same unit is correctly recorded.
E07 states that treatment unit costs for the system with an evaporation pond ranged up to 2.71 USD/m3; the upper bound value 2.71 is correctly captured.
E07 gives the treatment unit cost range in ‘USD/m3’; the recorded unit matches exactly.
E06 reports that total investment costs with evaporation ponds accounted for approximately 0.11% of the 2019 Thailand GDP; the value 0.11 is correctly extracted.
E06 explicitly gives the fraction as a percentage of GDP (‘0.11% ... of the 2019 Thailand GDP’); the unit ‘% of GDP’ accurately reflects this.

E05 describes that concentrate water has high concentrations of salt/impurities including PFAS; E06 discusses concentrate disposal by evaporation ponds and incineration of residual sediments. The statement accurately combines these author-reported points.

E06–E08 describe modeling of RO systems for all sanitary landfills in Thailand (111 sites) with national MSW and leachate volumes for policy planning, including an evaporation-pond option. This matches the description of a national-scale economic and system-design model including concentrate management.

E05 describes a two-pass RO system with pretreatment for LL; E05–E06 identify evaporation ponds for concentrate and incineration of residual sediments. The treatment description matches these details.

result.record_usable_rationale: All core elements—source identity, matrix (landfill leachate), treatment configuration (two-pass RO with evaporation ponds and incineration of sediments), study scale, and all quantitative economic findings—are directly supported by the cited text without numeric or unit errors. No contradictions were identified, so the record is usable for synthesis of RO-based PFAS residual management costs and configuration at national scale.
